note: Source of truth for the ATS résumé PDF. frontend/scripts/build-resume.mjs renders it to app/public/resume.pdf on every build; name, role and contact come from content.json so they cannot drift (set role here only to override the headline). Inside summary-level text, **double asterisks** mark a bold run — used for the claim a reader should catch when skimming; a highlight with no asterisks falls back to bolding the thesis up to the first colon. highlights renders as Career Highlights; an experience entry marked "earlier": true moves to the Earlier Experience section. An entry marked "keepTogether": true never splits across pages; one without it may split between bullets, and its title repeats with (continued) at the top of the next page. Page budget: two US Letter pages — any added line must be paid for. Voice: every bullet names the business problem, the decision or tradeoff, and the outcome. Length: the summary stays under six lines and every bullet under three; the long version lives on the site's Experience page.
location: Viña del Mar, Chile · Remote worldwide
summary: Cloud Architect and hands-on engineer, 13+ years building and running production systems, on AWS since 2014. I start from the business problem and make the tradeoffs explicit: at Electronic Payments I chose Magento as the storefront, moved orders, payments and POS sync into a distributed, event-driven middleware so nothing on the shop floor waits on the cloud, and standardized the platform as infrastructure as code. Founded Eleva, a multi-tenant SaaS on AWS, built end to end as a modular monolith.
highlights: **Built a complete SaaS product:** founded Eleva and, as its sole architect and engineer, took it from idea to production on AWS as a modular monolith. Won **Start-Up Chile Ignite (2022)**.
**Unified a retailer's online and in-store sales:** chose Magento as the almost-headless storefront; moved orders, payments and POS sync to an event-driven AWS middleware no register waits on.
**Changed how a company ships:** Magento was hard to deploy, so I standardized it as infrastructure as code (CDK) and built the **company's first CI/CD pipelines**, now reused by other projects.

experience.title: Lead Software Architect
bullets: Liquor Cart: **on-premise registers must keep selling when the cloud fails**. Chose Magento as the storefront; moved orders, payments and POS sync to an event-driven AWS middleware.

Built the .NET middleware for **resilience**: domain-driven services over RabbitMQ, retries, a replayable error queue, and a virtual host per store so a failure stays in that store. Wrote **about 90% of the C#**.
Preferred a custom event-sourced layer (Marten) over plugins for **security and traceability**: idempotent payment actions, tokenized card data, and attributable catalog and order changes.
Money and orders can disagree, so designed **payment recovery as a saga**: idempotent steps complete or cancel orders, void or refund payments, and escalate unresolved cases to a person.

Standardized hard-to-deploy Magento as **infrastructure as code (CDK)** with the **company's first CI/CD pipelines**: identical, auditable, schedulable and patchable environments from local to production.
Made the platform operable by the business: 40+ admin modules onboard **every new store, about 20,000 products, in around ten minutes**, and inspect or re-sync the integration without a developer.

Set **observability and security as defaults**: OpenTelemetry traces, alarms, least-privilege IAM, encrypted secrets. The architecture and pipelines became **reference implementations other projects reuse**.
Made a **six-person team** productive through conventions, reviews and mentoring, so juniors can touch production safely: 178 merged pull requests, **1,600+ unit tests on every push**.

experience.title: Founder and Platform Architect
bullets: **Designed, built and took the entire SaaS platform to production**: frontend, backend, data model, AWS infrastructure, automation and operations, ready to scale out on ECS Fargate.
Eleva runs whole-school staff evaluations: it generates a **200-person school's evaluations in about five minutes** and consolidates the school's progress in **under 20 seconds**.

Chose a **modular monolith** over microservices for a one-engineer platform: explicit module scopes and a multi-tenant configuration layer, so new features land as a module or tenant override, not a rewrite.
Evaluations affect careers, so a 360-degree process **freezes its configuration at creation**: results keep the rubric they were judged by, with per-school access scopes and evidence management.

Innovating with schools demanded agile delivery: environments as code (CDK) and CI/CD with ECS auto-rollback. **19 production deployments in 30 days, none failed**, each live in **about nine minutes**.

Designed for low operating cost: the .NET application tolerates scheduled shutdowns, so ECS and RDS stop outside school hours. An operations panel shows configuration drift and traces each release to its commit.
Folding AI in as an assistant, not a judge: it drafts feedback and summarizes evidence, while scores, stage transitions and reports stay deterministic and auditable.
